newsitem.title: USA: Venturian Napco stop work order rescinded.
newsitem.headline: Venturian Napco stop work order rescinded.

text.p: Venturian Corp said Wednesday that its Napco International Inc subsidiary has been notified that a stop-work order affecting an $11.6 million U.S. Army contract has been rescinded.

Venturian said the stop work order was issued in March based upon a competitor's protest of the contract award. It said the U.S. Army Tank-Automotive and Armaments Command's request to override the stop work issued in March was granted.

Venturian reported a first quarter net loss of $896,000 or $1.19 a share compared with $272,000 or $0.36 a share a year ago. Napco had a first-quarter operating loss of $213,000, compared with a year-ago operating profit of $429,000.

Gary Rappaport, Venturian president, said he was disappointed with Napco's first quarterly loss in several years, but was heartened by a substantially increased order backlog. Napco makes a variety of defense-related products.

The Venturian Software Inc subsidiary reported an operating loss of $488,000 in the 1997 first quarter, compared with a year-ago loss of $31,000. Rappaport said the widened loss reflected increased investment to market and support CyberCall, an Internet-Call Center software product for which the company has exclusive North American marketing rights.
